key_insight: Time-domain EEG representation learning can under-represent high-frequency signals because mean squared error favors larger, low-frequency components.
clinical_relevance: The findings may inform EEG biomarker research for brain disorders, but the abstract does not address cancer drug discovery or establish clinical utility.
method: Investigated three autoencoder architectures: LSTMVAE, VAEEG and Transformer.
Evaluated a state-of-the-art EEG foundation model.
Examined spectral bias and the effects of increasing latent dimensionality.
evidence_signal: Synthetic experiments and empirical validation showed that autoencoders captured broad changes such as alpha slowing while attenuating higher-frequency information; no numerical performance results are provided in the abstract.
watch_item: Larger latent representations reduced attenuation but compromised compactness and generative stability; spectral losses and gradient balancing are proposed directions rather than established solutions.
paper_title: Spectral Considerations on Unsupervised Time-domain EEG Representation Learning with Deep Networks
